title: How the ACTU Minimum Wage Increase Affects Your Annual Salary and Tax
description: Understand the ACTU minimum wage increase and how to convert your hourly rate to annual pay. Includes tax, Medicare, and super calculations for 2026-27.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours per week, the annual gross pay is approximately $52,244.48 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52. If you work a different number of hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

faqs.q: Does the ACTU minimum wage increase apply to casual employees?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum wage, so the casual rate is $33.05 per hour from 1 July 2026. The ACTU minimum wage increase campaign advocates for a higher base rate, but the loading is separate and paid on top of the applicable award or minimum rate.

faqs.q: How is tax calculated on my annual salary?
faqs.a: Use the 2026-27 resident tax brackets: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on $18,201–$45,000, 30% on $45,001–$135,000, 37% on $135,001–$190,000, and 45% above $190,000. Add the Medicare levy of 2% (unless you qualify for a reduction based on low income). This estimate does not include HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, converting between the two helps you compare jobs and plan your budget. The standard formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply that by 52 (the number of weeks in a year). For most full-time employees, the Fair Work Ombudsman assumes a 38-hour week, so the calculation becomes:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. A full-time employee on this rate earns:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,244.48 per year (before tax and super).

If you work more or fewer hours, adjust the weekly figure. The [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual equivalent instantly.

### The Role of Award Rates and the National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor set by the Fair Work Commission. Many employees are covered by industry or occupation awards that specify higher minimum rates. The ACTU minimum wage increase campaign pushes for a rise in this base rate to keep up with living costs. If you are on an award, your rate may be above the national minimum. Always check your award or enterprise agreement for your correct classification.

## Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, the next step is estimating tax. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) publishes resident tax rates for each financial year. For 2026-27, the brackets are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: 45% on the excess over $190,000

In addition, most residents pay the Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. Low-income earners may qualify for a reduction (using the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds as a guide, since 2026-27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate). For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage, the total tax plus Medicare levy would be:

$52,244.48 falls in the 30% bracket. Tax = 15% on $45,000 – $18,200 = $4,020 + 30% on $7,244.48 = $2,173.34? Let's calculate properly:

- Tax: nil on first $18,200 = $0
- 15% on $26,800 (45,000-18,200) = $4,020
- 30% on $7,244.48 = $2,173.34? Actually $52,244.48 - $45,000 = $7,244.48, 30% = $2,173.34? Wait: 30% of $7,244.48 = $2,173.34? Let's compute: $7,244.48 * 0.30 = $2,173.34. Total tax = $4,020 + $2,173 = $6,193. Then Medicare 2% = $1,044.89. Total tax + Medicare = $6,193 + $1,045 = $7,238. So about $7,238. So take-home after tax and Medicare is about $45,006. But this is an estimate.

Remember, this estimate does not include HELP, HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page provides more detail on deductions.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee contributions are paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. The rate from 1 July 2026 is 12% of your ordinary time earnings. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year (for the 2026-27 year). So if your annual gross is below that, super is 12% of that. For the minimum wage example, super = $52,244.48 × 12% = $6,269.34 per year, added to your super account. This is not part of your take-home pay.

### Casual Loading and Award Rates

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate. The Fair Work Ombudsman states that casual loading is meant to compensate for lack of paid leave. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading into the calculator; instead, use the base rate and check the casual loading box. The site will add 25% for you. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour.

## The ACTU Minimum Wage Increase and Its Impact

The ACTU minimum wage increase campaign calls for a meaningful rise in the National Minimum Wage to address cost-of-living pressures. Each year, the Fair Work Commission reviews the minimum wage and may increase it. The rate of $26.44 from 1 July 2026 reflects the most recent decision. If you are paid at or near the minimum, any increase directly lifts your annual salary. For example, a $1 per hour increase would add $1 × 38 × 52 = $1,976 per year. So a $1 increase adds about $1,976 per year. The ACTU advocates for a larger increase to close the gap between the minimum and living wage.

## Fortnightly Pay

Many employees are paid fortnightly. To get your fortnightly amount, divide your weekly pay by 2. For a full-time worker on the minimum wage, weekly gross = $1,004.90. Fortnightly = $2,009.80. This is useful for budgeting.

## Important Disclaimer

This article provides an estimate. Always consult a qualified professional for your specific situation. The [reference tables](/data) and [pay guides on this site provide more details.

### Summary

Use the formula hourly × hours per week × 52, assume 38 hours unless you have different hours. Distinguish National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and super paid on top. The ACTU minimum wage increase is a key factor in annual pay discussions.
